Security-and-audits page at docs.ipor.io lists two external audits: BlocSec (February 28, 2025) covering Fusion Vault, Base Fuses, Rewards Manager, Access Management, Price Oracle Middleware, Prehooks, Context Manager, Withdraw Manager; and Protofire (September 6, 2024) covering Fusion Vault, Base Fuses, Rewards Manager, Access Management, Price Oracle Middleware. Report PDFs are on Google Drive — direct PDF fetch was not attempted due to tool-call budget. Scope addresses not listed in audit pages (audit predates current factory-proxy deployment pattern).

GitHub repo https://github.com/IPOR-Labs/ipor-fusion confirmed via search results and docs. ipor-abi registry at https://github.com/IPOR-Labs/ipor-abi referenced as authoritative source for fuse addresses. No direct fetch of deployment broadcast files performed (tool-call budget exhausted); fuse addresses not recovered this run — recorded as D4/D6 unknowns.

Multi-chain factory proxies enumerated for 10 chains from the addresses doc (Ethereum, Unichain, TAC, Botanix, Base, Plasma, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Ink, Katana). Chains Hyperliquid L1, Robinhood Chain, Flare, Monad listed in protocol.chains but zero addresses surfaced — recorded as D5 unknowns. RobinhoodChain exceptions for multisig and operations wallet noted in governance doc.

IporFusionFactoryProxy is a factory — child vaults (PlasmaVaults) are deployed per-strategy per-chain. Cap notice: thousands of vaults possible; factory enumeration not attempted this run due to tool-call budget. Recorded as D6 unknown.

Role taxonomy applied: factory (IporFusionFactoryProxy x10 chains), proxy_admin (IporFusionFactoryImpl x10 chains — implementation, not callable), multisig (DAO Multisig 4-of-6, Operations wallet 4-of-6, IPOR Oracle multisig 3-of-5, IPOR DAO Snapshot 3-of-5), timelock (IPOR Protocol Timelock on Ethereum).

All admin_addresses[] entries traced to fetched URLs: factory addresses from docs.ipor.io/build-on-fusion/developer-guide/addresses.md; multisig addresses from docs.ipor.io/dao-governance/dao-governance/governing-multisig-wallets.md. PlasmaVault bytecode address 0xc2a119ea6de75e4b1451330321cb2474eb8d82d4 surfaced via search snippet only — recorded in unknowns, NOT in admin_addresses.

rationale.verdict: Walked official docs (addresses page, security/audits page, governance/multisig page), protocol website, and search results covering GitHub and Etherscan. Catalogued 10 IporFusionFactoryProxy addresses across 10 chains, 2 factory impl addresses (Ethereum and Base confirmed by implementation-slot reads per docs), plus 5 governance/admin addresses (DAO multisig, operations wallet, IPOR Protocol timelock, IPOR oracle multisig, IPOR DAO snapshot multisig). Fuse addresses, child PlasmaVault instances, and 4 chains (Hyperliquid L1, Robinhood Chain, Flare, Monad) remain uninspected.

protocol_metadata.about: Fusion by IPOR is an onchain vault infrastructure protocol that enables asset managers (called Atomists) and strategy executors (called Alphas) to deploy and manage ERC-4626-compliant Plasma Vaults. Users deposit assets into curated vaults that route capital to integrated DeFi protocols (Aave, Morpho, SparkLend, Euler, and others) via a modular system of Fuses — adapters that scope vault interactions to whitelisted markets. Each vault operates with isolated risk, configurable access management via OpenZeppelin's AccessManager, fee timelocks, and optional depositor-led governance through Aragon DAOs, making it suitable for both retail and institutional yield strategies.
